## What changed

**Nothing. Not the skill's behaviour on this task, and not the score.** This is the task cap-evolve's
`RESULT` line names as broken by the accepted champion:

> ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.962 Δ=+0.086 · fixed={…} · broke={**bench-aap2-006-log-root-cause**,
> bench-aap2-008-preceding-task}

Measured at equal `n`, that verdict is false. Inside the same iteration:

- the seed, re-measured at `n=9`, scored **0.777778**
- `cand_0001`, at `n=9`, scored **0.777778**

**Identical to six decimal places.** The delta at equal `n` is `0.000`. The `−0.222` the run reports
is the difference between a *reused* `n=3` `seed` value of `1.000` and an `n=9` candidate — that is,
it is entirely a sampling artifact. The `n=3` val sample drew three trials from a distribution whose
`n=9` mode is `0.750`, and got three ceilings.

This task also has no errored trials in either cell, so nothing about the comparison is confounded by
harness loss. It is simply the same number twice.

## What worked

**The answer, every single time, for both artifacts.** With weights `0.5 / 0.5`, two expected tool
calls and three required facts, the observed values have unique solutions:

| observed | expected calls matched | answer facts | seed @ n=9 | `cand_0001` @ n=9 |
|--:|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| 0.750 | **1 of 2** | 3 of 3 | 8 | 8 |
| 1.000 | 2 of 2 | 3 of 3 | 1 | 1 |

The agent named the right job (`90520`, the recent one — not the `90521` distractor), the right root
cause, and the expiry date `2026-07-18`, on **18 of 18 trials**. It missed one of the two expected
tool calls on 16 of 18.

That matters because the scenario was built to catch exactly the failure it never produced. Its stated
purpose is to "discriminate agents that read the most recent failed run vs. the first match in the
result set" — job `90521` is a week older, is also a certificate-rotation failure on `prod1`, and fails
for a different reason ("connection refused"). An agent that grabs it "answers about a completely
different cause and misses the expiry-date fact entirely." **No trial ever did.** The distractor was
never taken.

## What didn't

**`per_task_scores.csv`'s note on this task is wrong, and the decomposition shows it.** The note reads:

> No improvement — persistent assertion mismatch

There is no assertion mismatch. The answer component was **3 of 3 on every trial in both cells**. The
persistent `0.25` shortfall is a **tool-call** shortfall — one of the two calls the contract names,
missed on 16 of 18 trials by both the seed and the champion alike. The hand-written note attributes a
stable, fully explained tool-sequencing gap to the answer half of the reward. It is recorded here
rather than silently corrected in the CSV, because the CSV is a verbatim copy of the source analysis;
the correction belongs in the reading, not in the artifact.

**The contract itself has a suspicious asymmetry** worth checking before this task is scored again:
`n_expected_calls` is **2** while `n_golden_tool_calls` is **3**. The golden path makes three calls;
the contract scores against two. That is the only task in v2 where those disagree, and it sits on the
one task where every trial loses exactly half the call credit. Whether the missing call is one the
agent should reasonably make, or one the extraction picked up from a golden path that does more than
the contract asks, is answerable from `results/v2/tasks.json` and `expected.json` in about a minute —
and it is a far better use of time than another skill edit.

**The `0.25` from iteration 1 is a different animal.** `run_20260816_202942`'s rejected `cand_0001`
scored `[1.000, 1.000, 0.250]` here, and the CSV calls that trial a **"one-trial flake."** It
decomposes to `1 of 2` calls and **0 of 3** facts — the only trial in this task's entire history where
the answer was wrong. The framework's `RESULT` for that iteration also named this task under
`broke={}`. With one trial and no rollout read, "flake" is a label, not a diagnosis.

## What we can (or can't) learn

**The load-bearing lesson is about the verdict, not the task.** This is the cleanest counterexample in
the branch to reading cap-evolve's `fixed`/`broke` lists as facts about candidates. Two tasks appear
under `broke={}` in this run. At equal `n`, this one is **exactly flat** and
[`008`](v2-bench-aap2-008-preceding-task.md) is **+0.133 — an improvement**. Both entries are wrong,
and both are wrong for the same structural reason: the run gated an `n=9` candidate against an `n=3`
baseline it reused instead of re-measuring (`--reuse-baseline`), so every per-task verdict is a
comparison between different trial counts. See `results/v2/summary.md`.

**We can also learn that this scenario's honest design cost is visible and was worth paying.** The
author wanted a forbidden fact `no-wrong-run-cause` forbidding "connection refused", but that string
lives in job `90521`'s log in the seed, so the required-present / forbidden-absent gate would have
failed on `forbidden-absent`. The recorded decision — **"forbidden fact omitted; distractor job
retained"** — kept the discriminating distractor and relied on the `expiry-date` required fact to catch
a wrong-run answer instead. Eighteen trials later, `expiry-date` was never missed, so the substitution
held. That is a design trade-off documented before the run and then vindicated by it, which is rarer
than it should be.

**What we cannot say is anything about whether the champion helped or hurt here.** It did neither, at
`n=9`, to six decimal places. The only open question on this task is the contract's `2`-vs-`3` call
count, and that is a question for the benchmark author, not the optimizer.
